findings.finding: The audit HTML renderer (src/rebar/audit/templates/_completion.html, fed by src/rebar/audit/page.py `_completion_section` which reads the completion sidecar/attestation record the plan modifies) is an unenumerated per-criterion rendering consumer. Its FAIL branch hard-codes an 'unmet' ✗ glyph per finding (:23) and its PASS branch renders per-criterion met/unmet glyphs (:10) — an insufficient-evidence (`evidence_sufficient:false`) entry would render as a bare 'unmet' ✗ in the audit UI, reproducing the absence-of-evidence-as-refutation misattribution the plan aims to eliminate. The plan's edit-set and its 'both rendering seams' AC name only the CLI (`_render_verdict_text`) and close-gate renderers.
findings.location: Full consumer graph / Scope; AC 'Both rendering seams emit ...'
scenarios: A ticket whose completion verdict banks an insufficient-evidence entry is viewed in the audit UI — the criterion shows a plain 'unmet' ✗, not 'insufficient evidence', undercutting the fix
findings.suggested_fix: Enumerate src/rebar/audit/page.py `_completion_section` and src/rebar/audit/templates/_completion.html as a rendering consumer; surface `evidence_sufficient:false` there (distinct glyph/label = 'insufficient evidence' rather than 'unmet' ✗), and broaden the 'both rendering seams' AC to name all three renderers.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Name the concrete discriminator that lets upsert/harvest tell a genuine refutation (replace marker) from a marker-preserving re-harvest, given both arrive as (cid, met=false) with no model-supplied marker (e.g. gate on source='harvest' vs 'tool', or only fallback_record ever clears/sets the marker).
evidence: harvest calls `bank.upsert(str(cid), bool(record['met']), ..., source='harvest')` — always met=false for an unmet criterion
Plan: 'genuine refutation (bare met=false) replaces it' vs 'overwrite retains the prior entry's marker' — same upsert inputs for both
Plan states 'the marker is never a model-tool input', so nothing in the harvested record signals which case applies
findings.finding: The plan's rule 'a genuine refutation (bare met=false) replaces [the marker]' cannot be distinguished from a marker-preserving re-harvest at the write path: harvest_structured_into_bank ALWAYS calls upsert(cid, bool(met=false), ...) for an unmet criterion, and the marker is framework-set / never a model input, so a harvested refutation and a re-harvest that should preserve an insufficient marker present an IDENTICAL (cid, met=false, no-marker) signature. The plan names no discriminator (e.g. source='harvest' vs 'tool').
scenarios: An insufficient (marker) entry is re-harvested when the model later emits met=false for the same criterion: is that a genuine refutation (replace) or a stale echo (preserve)? The write path cannot tell, so one of the two AC bullets is violated.
findings.suggested_fix: Restrict marker-setting to fallback_record (source='tool' bounded fallback) and make harvest (source='harvest') a met=false that always clears the marker (genuine refutation), so the source field is the discriminator; state this explicitly in the plan.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify WHERE preserve-on-overwrite reads the prior entry's marker (add a read-modify-write in upsert, or make harvest read bank.get(cid) and re-pass the marker), since upsert currently blind-writes a fresh dict with no prior read.
evidence: upsert body (451-461) constructs `entry = {...}` from scratch and writes it unconditionally; no `self.get(criterion_id)` read precedes it
Plan: 'harvest sources it by PRESERVATION: overwrite retains the prior entry's marker'
Preservation requires reading the existing entry before overwrite — a mechanism the current blind-write upsert lacks
findings.finding: The plan relies on 'preserve-on-overwrite' — harvest retaining a prior entry's evidence_sufficient marker — but CriterionBank.upsert (completion_banking.py:451-461) builds a fresh entry dict and blind-writes it with no read of the prior entry. Preservation is a NEW read-modify-write behavior the plan presents as a natural property without specifying where the prior-marker read occurs (inside upsert vs at the harvest call site).
findings.location: Proposed fix — harvest_structured_into_bank preservation clause; completion_banking.py:441-461, :563-591
scenarios: A fallback banks evidence_sufficient:false at exhaustion; a later successor re-harvest calls upsert for the same criterion; the fresh dict has no marker and silently drops it, re-introducing the very false-FAIL the fix targets
findings.suggested_fix: Have upsert read the existing entry and carry forward its evidence_sufficient marker when the incoming write does not set one; document that a bare met=false explicitly clears it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the per-record sufficiency field the finalizer's banked_evidence payload carries (name + shape) and the prompt decision rule (:23-28) that keys insufficient-vs-unmet findings text on it, so the finalizer can distinguish exhaustion from refutation from its own input.
evidence: Plan: 'banked insufficient entries echo as met:false with insufficient findings text; merge_finalizer_with_bank re-stamps the marker from the bank (stamp = enforcement, prompt = text alignment)'
Current prompt line 26: 'Include one high-severity finding for every criterion with met:false' — uniform, no insufficient/refuted split
_run_finalizer payload records omit any sufficiency marker: {criterion_id, met, evidence, truncated} (completion_recovery.py:739-744)
AC line says '_run_finalizer payload carries the marker (:741)' but the prompt-rule item does not name the per-record field or the decision rule keyed on it
findings.finding: The finalizer prompt rule change (:23-28) tells the LLM to echo insufficient banked entries as met:false with distinct 'insufficient findings text', but does not specify HOW the finalizer distinguishes an insufficient entry from a genuinely-refuted one in its input, nor the per-record field it keys on. The finalizer is a tool-free LLM whose banked_evidence records currently carry only criterion_id/met/evidence/truncated (completion_recovery.py:738-746); differentiated findings text requires a per-record marker in the finalizer's input AND a prompt decision rule reading it.
findings.location: Plan: 'Finalizer prompt' bullet + completion_verifier_finalizer.md:23-28; completion_recovery.py:738-746 (_run_finalizer banked_evidence build)
scenarios: Author edits the prompt to emit insufficient text but the finalizer cannot tell which of its met:false records are exhaustion vs refutation, so it guesses or applies it uniformly
The re-stamp masks the mismatch on the merge path, but a deterministic-fallback or direct-finalizer render shows finalizer-authored text that contradicts the re-stamped class
findings.suggested_fix: Add to the plan: the _run_finalizer banked_evidence record gains an explicit per-entry sufficiency marker (mirroring the bank field), and the finalizer prompt rule reads that marker to choose 'insufficient-evidence' finding text for marker-carrying met:false entries vs 'not demonstrated' for bare met:false.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the Context (implies false FAIL verdicts should be corrected) with the fix (keeps FAIL, blocks, relabels only): state explicitly that honest classification is the goal and name the downstream consumer (if any) that uses `evidence_sufficient:false` to trigger retry/unblock, or note that unblocking is out of scope.
evidence: Context: 'misattributing absence-of-evidence as evidence-of-absence, producing false FAIL verdicts on tickets whose evidence exists but was not reached within the window.'
Close-gate bullet: 'still gates on non-PASS (fail-closed)'
Banked-entry rendering bullet: 'Honesty of message and recorded class, never gate leniency.'
findings.finding: The Context/Problem frames the defect as 'producing false FAIL verdicts on tickets whose evidence exists but was not reached within the window,' implying the erroneous FAIL should be corrected. The fix, however, explicitly preserves the FAIL verdict and blocking behavior ('still gates on non-PASS (fail-closed)', 'Honesty of message and recorded class, never gate leniency') — changing only the classification/message, not the outcome. A ticket whose evidence exists but was unreached still fails to close. The plan does not reconcile whether relabeling alone resolves the stated problem, or whether a downstream unblock/retry path is expected to consume the marker.
findings.location: Context / Problem vs. reconcile_verdict / close-gate refusal bullets
findings.suggested_fix: Add a sentence to Context/Problem or Scope clarifying that the verdict deliberately stays FAIL/blocking and the marker only corrects the recorded class and remediation text (enabling a future retry policy, cited as out-of-scope), so the 'false FAIL' framing is about misclassification, not about unblocking closure.

Plan: 'merge_finalizer_with_bank re-stamps the marker from the bank (stamp = enforcement, prompt = text alignment)' — implies the model should not author it, but never says the prompt tells the model to omit it
verdict_obtainable schema note establishes 'never model-supplied' as the precedent for the same class of marker (schema :16)
findings.finding: The plan does not state whether the finalizer prompt must instruct the model to OMIT evidence_sufficient from its own output (since the marker is framework-set/never-model-supplied and merge_finalizer_with_bank is the authoritative re-stamp). The finalizer emits the full completion_verdict schema, which now permits evidence_sufficient; without an explicit omit instruction the model may emit the marker and create a pink-elephant / stamp-vs-model-output ambiguity that only the merge path silently overrides.
scenarios: The finalizer, seeing evidence_sufficient in the schema it validates against, emits it on some criterion; the re-stamp only runs on the merge path, so a direct-render or a criterion the merge existing-record branch keeps could surface a model-authored marker of unknown provenance
